```{r function-correct_accent}
#' A function to remove accented characters from all the character values of a data frame
#'
#' @param data Dataframe, usually the DHIS2 immunization dataframe
#' @param pattern A character value to match or a regular expression. Default "Ã©|Ã©"
#' @param replacement A character value to replace the pattern. Default "e"
#'
#' @return
#' A dataframe with values corrected
#' @export
#'
#' @examples
correct_accent <- function(data, pattern = "\u00C3\u00A9", replacement = "e") {
  variables <- colnames(data)

  # UTF-8 characters decoded as Latin-1 (mojibake) commonly seen in DHIS 2
  # exports, e.g. "Août" read as "AoÃ»t" or "Février" read as "FÃ©vrier".
  mojibake <- c(
    "\u00C3\u0080" = "A", "\u00C3\u0082" = "A", "\u00C3\u0084" = "A", "\u00C3\u0085" = "A",
    "\u00C3\u0087" = "C", "\u00C3\u0088" = "E", "\u00C3\u0089" = "E", "\u00C3\u008A" = "E",
    "\u00C3\u008B" = "E", "\u00C3\u008E" = "I", "\u00C3\u008F" = "I", "\u00C3\u0091" = "N",
    "\u00C3\u0092" = "O", "\u00C3\u0094" = "O", "\u00C3\u0096" = "O", "\u00C3\u0099" = "U",
    "\u00C3\u009B" = "U", "\u00C3\u009C" = "U",
    "\u00C3\u00A0" = "a", "\u00C3\u00A2" = "a", "\u00C3\u00A3" = "a", "\u00C3\u00A4" = "a",
    "\u00C3\u00A5" = "a", "\u00C3\u00A7" = "c", "\u00C3\u00A8" = "e", "\u00C3\u00A9" = "e",
    "\u00C3\u00AA" = "e", "\u00C3\u00AB" = "e", "\u00C3\u00AC" = "i", "\u00C3\u00AE" = "i",
    "\u00C3\u00AF" = "i", "\u00C3\u00B1" = "n", "\u00C3\u00B2" = "o", "\u00C3\u00B4" = "o",
    "\u00C3\u00B6" = "o", "\u00C3\u00B9" = "u", "\u00C3\u00BB" = "u", "\u00C3\u00BC" = "u",
    "\u00C3\u00BF" = "y"
  )

  data_list <- Map(function(x) {
    out <- data[[x]]
    out <- gsub(pattern, replacement, out)
    for (i in seq_along(mojibake)) out <- gsub(names(mojibake)[i], mojibake[i], out)
    out
  }, variables)

  data <- as.data.frame(data_list)

  colnames(data) <- tolower(gsub("\\.", "_", colnames(data)))
  for (i in seq_along(mojibake)) colnames(data) <- gsub(names(mojibake)[i], mojibake[i], colnames(data))

  return(data)
}


```

# Outlier detection

```{r function-flag_outliers}
#' Flag outlying monthly vaccination counts
#'
#' For every unit of the chosen level and every vaccine, the monthly number of
#' vaccinated children is compared only with the other months of that same unit.
#' Five standard statistical rules are computed side by side and every
#' statistic is returned, so the reason a month is flagged can be audited.
#' Only base R is used.
#'
#' Monthly counts are the differences between consecutive cumulative totals
#' from \code{\link{vaccine_sums}}, so the columns summed for each vaccine are
#' exactly those used for the coverage computation.
#'
#' The rules, all applied to the unit's own monthly series:
#' \itemize{
#'   \item \strong{iqr}: Tukey fences, Q1 - k*IQR and Q3 + k*IQR (k = 1.5).
#'   \item \strong{adjbox}: adjusted boxplot of Hubert and Vandervieren (2008). The fences are
#'     skewed with the medcouple, which suits count data that are not symmetric.
#'   \item \strong{zscore}: leave-one-out z-score. The month is compared with the mean and SD of the
#'     unit's other months, so an extreme value cannot inflate the SD and hide itself (|z| > 3).
#'   \item \strong{mad}: modified z-score of Iglewicz and Hoaglin, 0.6745 * (x - median) / MAD (|M| > 3.5).
#'   \item \strong{gesd}: generalized extreme Studentized deviate test of Rosner (1983), which finds
#'     up to several outliers while controlling the type I error (alpha = 0.05).
#' }
#' A month is flagged by a rule when it is outside that rule's limits and at least \code{min_diff}
#' away from the unit's median (so tiny fluctuations in small units are ignored). The final
#' \code{flagged} column is TRUE when at least \code{min_methods} rules agree.
#'
#' @param data Dataframe, the DHIS2 immunization dataframe (as passed to \code{vaccine_sums}).
#' @param level The aggregation level of interest, specified as in \code{vaccine_sums}:
#'   Country, Province, District, Aire, Fosa, Antenne, or a combination such as c(Antenne, District).
#' @param vaccine Character vector of vaccine names (see \code{vaccine_sums}). NULL (default) uses
#'   every vaccine the package knows.
#' @param months Integer vector of months to consider. Months in which no unit reports any dose
#'   of the vaccine are ignored. Default 1:12.
#' @param min_methods Number of rules (out of 5) that must flag a month for \code{flagged} to be TRUE.
#'   Default 2.
#' @param flagged_only If TRUE (default) only flagged months are returned; if FALSE every
#'   unit-vaccine-month is returned with its statistics.
#' @param k_iqr Multiplier of the IQR fences. Default 1.5.
#' @param z_cut Cutoff of the leave-one-out z-score. Default 3.
#' @param mad_cut Cutoff of the modified z-score. Default 3.5.
#' @param alpha Significance level of the GESD test. Default 0.05.
#' @param min_diff Minimum absolute difference from the unit's median for a rule to flag a month.
#'   Default 20.
#' @param min_months Minimum number of reporting months needed to assess a unit. Default 5.
#' @param accent Passed to \code{vaccine_sums}. Default FALSE (data already cleaned).
#'
#' @return A dataframe with one row per unit, vaccine and month containing: the unit column(s),
#'   vaccine, month, value (monthly count), the series statistics (n, median, mean_other,
#'   sd_other, q1, q3, iqr, mad, medcouple), ratio_median (value / median), each rule's
#'   statistic and limits (iqr_lower, iqr_upper, adjbox_lower, adjbox_upper, z_loo, mod_z,
#'   gesd_stat, gesd_crit), one logical flag per rule (flag_iqr, flag_adjbox, flag_zscore, flag_mad,
#'   flag_gesd), n_flags, flagged and direction ("high", "low" or NA). Sorted by n_flags and
#'   relative distance from the median.
#' @export
#'
#' @references
#' Hubert M, Vandervieren E (2008). An adjusted boxplot for skewed distributions.
#' Computational Statistics and Data Analysis 52:5186-5201.
#'
#' Iglewicz B, Hoaglin D (1993). How to detect and handle outliers. ASQC Quality Press.
#'
#' Rosner B (1983). Percentage points for a generalized ESD many-outlier procedure.
#' Technometrics 25:165-172.
#'
#' @examples
#' \dontrun{
#' flag_outliers(ri, District, vaccine = c("DTC1", "Pneumo13"), months = 1:9)
#' flag_outliers(ri, c(Antenne, District), months = 1:9, min_methods = 3)
#' flag_outliers(ri, District, vaccine = "BCG", flagged_only = FALSE)
#' }
flag_outliers <- function(data, level, vaccine = NULL, months = 1:12,
                          min_methods = 2, flagged_only = TRUE,
                          k_iqr = 1.5, z_cut = 3, mad_cut = 3.5, alpha = 0.05,
                          min_diff = 20, min_months = 5, accent = FALSE) {
  all_vacc <- c(
    "BCG", "DTC1", "DTC2", "DTC3", "VPO0", "VPO1", "VPO2", "VPO3", "VAA",
    "VAR1", "VAR2", "VPI1", "VPI2", "Pneumo13", "Pneumo13_2", "Rota1",
    "Rota2", "Rota3", "VAP1", "VAP2", "VAP3", "VAP4", "TD2"
  )
  unit <- c(
    "Country" = "orgunitlevel1", "Province" = "orgunitlevel2", "District" = "orgunitlevel3",
    "Aire" = "orgunitlevel4", "Fosa" = "orgunitlevel5", "Antenne" = "orgunitlevel6"
  )

  level_expr <- substitute(level)
  level_cols <- eval(level_expr, stats::setNames(as.list(unit), names(unit)), parent.frame())

  months <- sort(unique(as.integer(months)))
  stopifnot(
    is.data.frame(data), all(level_cols %in% unit), all(months %in% 1:12),
    is.numeric(min_methods), min_methods >= 1, min_methods <= 5,
    is.logical(flagged_only), length(flagged_only) == 1,
    is.numeric(k_iqr), k_iqr > 0, is.numeric(z_cut), z_cut > 0,
    is.numeric(mad_cut), mad_cut > 0, is.numeric(alpha), alpha > 0, alpha < 1,
    is.numeric(min_diff), min_diff >= 0, is.numeric(min_months), min_months >= 4
  )
  if (is.null(vaccine)) vaccine <- all_vacc
  stopifnot(is.character(vaccine), all(vaccine %in% all_vacc))

  results <- list()

  for (v in vaccine) {
    cumul <- tryCatch(
      lapply(months, function(m) {
        s <- eval(bquote(vaccine_sums(data, .(as.name(v)), .(level_expr), .(m), accent = .(accent))))
        s$.month <- m
        s
      }),
      error = function(e) {
        message("Skipping ", v, ": ", conditionMessage(e))
        NULL
      }
    )
    if (is.null(cumul)) next

    wide <- Reduce(function(a, b) merge(a, b, by = level_cols, all = TRUE), lapply(cumul, function(s) {
      out <- s[, c(level_cols, v)]
      names(out)[names(out) == v] <- paste0("m", s$.month[1])
      out
    }))
    mat <- as.matrix(wide[, paste0("m", months), drop = FALSE])
    mat[is.na(mat)] <- 0

    monthly <- mat
    if (ncol(mat) > 1) monthly[, -1] <- mat[, -1, drop = FALSE] - mat[, -ncol(mat), drop = FALSE]
    colnames(monthly) <- months

    reporting <- colSums(monthly) > 0
    if (sum(reporting) < min_months) next
    monthly <- monthly[, reporting, drop = FALSE]

    per_unit <- lapply(seq_len(nrow(monthly)), function(i) {
      x <- monthly[i, ]
      st <- .outlier_stats(x, k_iqr, z_cut, mad_cut, alpha)
      st$month <- as.integer(names(x))
      st$value <- unname(x)
      st$unit_row <- i
      st
    })
    per_unit <- do.call(rbind, per_unit)
    per_unit$vaccine <- v
    results[[length(results) + 1]] <- cbind(wide[per_unit$unit_row, level_cols, drop = FALSE], per_unit)
  }

  cols <- c(
    level_cols, "vaccine", "month", "value", "n", "median", "mean_other", "sd_other",
    "q1", "q3", "iqr", "mad", "medcouple", "ratio_median", "iqr_lower", "iqr_upper",
    "adjbox_lower", "adjbox_upper", "z_loo", "mod_z", "gesd_stat", "gesd_crit",
    "flag_iqr", "flag_adjbox", "flag_zscore", "flag_mad", "flag_gesd",
    "n_flags", "flagged", "direction"
  )

  if (length(results) == 0) {
    out <- as.data.frame(matrix(NA, 0, length(cols)))
    names(out) <- cols
    return(out)
  }

  out <- do.call(rbind, results)
  far <- abs(out$value - out$median) >= min_diff
  flag_cols <- c("flag_iqr", "flag_adjbox", "flag_zscore", "flag_mad", "flag_gesd")
  for (f in flag_cols) out[[f]] <- out[[f]] & far
  out$n_flags <- rowSums(out[, flag_cols])
  out$flagged <- out$n_flags >= min_methods
  out$direction <- ifelse(out$n_flags > 0, ifelse(out$value > out$median, "high", "low"), NA_character_)
  out$ratio_median <- round(out$value / out$median, 3)

  if (flagged_only) out <- out[out$flagged, ]
  out <- out[order(-out$n_flags, -abs(out$value - out$median) / pmax(out$median, 1)), cols]
  rownames(out) <- NULL
  out
}

.outlier_stats <- function(x, k_iqr, z_cut, mad_cut, alpha) {
  n <- length(x)
  med <- stats::median(x)
  q <- stats::quantile(x, c(0.25, 0.75), names = FALSE, type = 7)
  iqr <- q[2] - q[1]
  madv <- stats::mad(x, constant = 1)

  s <- sum(x)
  m_other <- (s - x) / (n - 1)
  var_other <- pmax((sum(x^2) - x^2 - (n - 1) * m_other^2) / (n - 2), 0)
  sd_other <- sqrt(var_other)
  z_loo <- (x - m_other) / sd_other
  z_loo[sd_other == 0] <- ifelse(x[sd_other == 0] == m_other[sd_other == 0], 0, Inf * sign(x - m_other)[sd_other == 0])

  mod_z <- if (madv > 0) {
    0.6745 * (x - med) / madv
  } else {
    meanad <- mean(abs(x - med))
    if (meanad > 0) (x - med) / (1.253314 * meanad) else rep(0, n)
  }

  mc <- .medcouple(x)
  if (mc >= 0) {
    adj_l <- q[1] - k_iqr * exp(-4 * mc) * iqr
    adj_u <- q[2] + k_iqr * exp(3 * mc) * iqr
  } else {
    adj_l <- q[1] - k_iqr * exp(-3 * mc) * iqr
    adj_u <- q[2] + k_iqr * exp(4 * mc) * iqr
  }
  iqr_l <- q[1] - k_iqr * iqr
  iqr_u <- q[2] + k_iqr * iqr

  g <- .gesd(x, alpha)

  data.frame(
    n = n, median = med, mean_other = round(m_other, 2), sd_other = round(sd_other, 2),
    q1 = q[1], q3 = q[2], iqr = iqr, mad = madv, medcouple = round(mc, 3),
    ratio_median = NA_real_,
    iqr_lower = iqr_l, iqr_upper = iqr_u,
    adjbox_lower = round(adj_l, 2), adjbox_upper = round(adj_u, 2),
    z_loo = round(z_loo, 2), mod_z = round(mod_z, 2),
    gesd_stat = round(g$stat, 2), gesd_crit = round(g$crit, 2),
    flag_iqr = x < iqr_l | x > iqr_u,
    flag_adjbox = x < adj_l | x > adj_u,
    flag_zscore = abs(z_loo) > z_cut,
    flag_mad = abs(mod_z) > mad_cut,
    flag_gesd = g$flag,
    row.names = NULL
  )
}

.medcouple <- function(x) {
  med <- stats::median(x)
  lo <- x[x <= med]
  hi <- x[x >= med]
  h <- outer(hi, lo, function(xj, xi) ifelse(xj - xi == 0, NA, ((xj - med) - (med - xi)) / (xj - xi)))
  h <- h[!is.na(h)]
  if (length(h) == 0) 0 else stats::median(h)
}

.gesd <- function(x, alpha) {
  n <- length(x)
  r <- max(1, floor(n / 3))
  idx <- seq_len(n)
  removed <- integer(0)
  stat <- crit <- rep(NA_real_, r)
  keep <- idx
  for (i in seq_len(r)) {
    xs <- x[keep]
    sdv <- stats::sd(xs)
    if (!is.finite(sdv) || sdv == 0) break
    dev <- abs(xs - mean(xs))
    j <- which.max(dev)
    stat[i] <- dev[j] / sdv
    p <- 1 - alpha / (2 * (n - i + 1))
    t <- stats::qt(p, n - i - 1)
    crit[i] <- (n - i) * t / sqrt((n - i - 1 + t^2) * (n - i + 1))
    removed <- c(removed, keep[j])
    keep <- keep[-j]
  }
  k <- which(stat > crit)
  k <- if (length(k)) max(k) else 0
  flag <- rep(FALSE, n)
  if (k > 0) flag[removed[seq_len(k)]] <- TRUE
  st <- crit_v <- rep(NA_real_, n)
  st[removed] <- stat[seq_along(removed)]
  crit_v[removed] <- crit[seq_along(removed)]
  list(flag = flag, stat = st, crit = crit_v)
}
```

```{r tests-flag_outliers}
test_that("flag_outliers flags a data-entry error within its own unit", {
  months <- c("Janvier", "Fevrier", "Mars", "Avril", "Mai", "Juin", "Juillet", "Aout", "Septembre")
  df <- data.frame(
    periodname = rep(paste(months, 2026), 2),
    orgunitlevel1 = "Pays", orgunitlevel2 = "p",
    orgunitlevel3 = rep(c("kn A Zone de Sante", "kn B Zone de Sante"), each = 9),
    bcg_0_et_11_mois = c(300, 310, 295, 305, 3905, 298, 302, 311, 300, rep(500, 9) + c(0, 5, -5, 3, -3, 2, -2, 4, -4))
  )
  out <- flag_outliers(df, District, vaccine = "BCG", months = 1:9)
  expect_equal(nrow(out), 1)
  expect_equal(out$orgunitlevel3, "kn A Zone de Sante")
  expect_equal(out$month, 5L)
  expect_equal(out$direction, "high")
  expect_equal(out$n_flags, 5)
  all_rows <- flag_outliers(df, District, vaccine = "BCG", months = 1:9, flagged_only = FALSE)
  expect_equal(nrow(all_rows), 18)
  expect_true(all(c("z_loo", "mod_z", "gesd_stat", "iqr_lower", "adjbox_upper", "medcouple") %in% names(all_rows)))
  expect_equal(sum(all_rows$value[all_rows$orgunitlevel3 == "kn A Zone de Sante"]), 300+310+295+305+3905+298+302+311+300)
  expect_equal(nrow(flag_outliers(df, District, vaccine = "BCG", months = 1:9, min_methods = 5)), 1)
  expect_error(flag_outliers(df, District, vaccine = "nope"))
})
```

# VAP introduction dates

```{r function-vap_start_month}
#' First month of the year in which a VAP dose can be counted for each health district
#'
#' @param orgunitlevel3 Character vector of health district names, as in the DHIS2 data or in the target populations. Accents, case and punctuation are ignored when matching.
#' @param vap_intro A dataframe with the columns orgunitlevel3, intro_year and intro_month, as the built-in vap_intro dataset.
#' @param year The calendar year of the data.
#' @return
#' A numeric vector the length of orgunitlevel3. 1 if the district introduced VAP before year, the introduction month if it introduced it during year, and Inf if it introduces it after year, has not introduced it, or is not in the VAP pyramid.
#' @noRd
vap_start_month <- function(orgunitlevel3, vap_intro, year = 2026) {
  unit_key <- function(x) {
    x <- gsub("[^a-z0-9]+", "_", tolower(iconv(as.character(x), to = "ASCII//TRANSLIT")))
    gsub("^_|_$", "", x)
  }
  stopifnot(all(c("orgunitlevel3", "intro_year", "intro_month") %in% names(vap_intro)))
  pos <- match(unit_key(orgunitlevel3), unit_key(vap_intro[["orgunitlevel3"]]))
  yr <- vap_intro[["intro_year"]][pos]
  mo <- vap_intro[["intro_month"]][pos]
  start <- ifelse(yr < year, 1, ifelse(yr == year, mo, Inf))
  start[is.na(start)] <- Inf
  start
}
```

```{r tests-vap_vaccines}
test_that("VAP sums and coverage respect the introduction dates", {
  vi <- data.frame(
    orgunitlevel2 = "kn Province",
    orgunitlevel3 = c("kn A Zone de Sante", "kn B Zone de Sante", "kn C Zone de Sante"),
    in_pyramid = TRUE, intro_year = c(2025L, 2026L, NA), intro_month = c(8L, 3L, NA)
  )
  df <- data.frame(
    periodname = rep(c("Janvier 2026", "Fevrier 2026", "Mars 2026", "Avril 2026"), 3),
    orgunitlevel1 = "Pays", orgunitlevel2 = "kn Province",
    orgunitlevel3 = rep(vi$orgunitlevel3, each = 4),
    b_8_4_vap_1_0_et_11_mois__fixe = 10
  )
  s <- vaccine_sums(df, VAP1, District, month = 4, accent = FALSE, vap_intro = vi)
  expect_equal(s$VAP1, c(40, 20, 0))
  s_all <- vaccine_sums(df, VAP1, District, month = 4, accent = FALSE, vap_intro = NULL)
  expect_equal(s_all$VAP1, c(40, 40, 40))
  pops <- data.frame(
    orgunitlevel1 = "Pays", orgunitlevel2 = "kn Province", orgunitlevel3 = vi$orgunitlevel3,
    survivants_mois_admin = 10, survivant_mois_ajust = 20
  )
  cov <- vaccine_coverage(s, VAP1, District, month = 4, pops = pops, vap_intro = vi)
  expect_equal(cov$VAP1_admin, c(100, 100, NA))
  expect_equal(cov$VAP1_ajust, c(50, 50, NA))
  expect_true(all(c("vap_survivants_mois_admin", "vap_survivant_mois_ajust") %in% names(cov)))
  expect_false("survivants_mois_admin" %in% names(cov))
  cov_c <- vaccine_coverage(vaccine_sums(df, VAP1, Country, month = 4, accent = FALSE, vap_intro = vi), VAP1, Country, month = 4, pops = pops, vap_intro = vi)
  expect_equal(cov_c$VAP1_admin, round(100 * 60 / (40 + 20), 2))
})
```

# Tally of vaccinated 


```{r function-vaccine_sums}
#' A function to compute the cummulative monthly tally of vaccinated per organization levels using DHIS2 exported data
#'
#' @param data Dataframe, usually the DHIS2 immunization dataframe
#' @param vaccine Column name of the vaccine of interest. Should be one of the following: BCG, DTC1, DTC3, VPO0, VAA, VAR1, VAR2, VPI1, VPI2, Pneumo13, Rota1, Rota2, Rota3, VAP1, VAP2, VAP3, VAP4, DTC2, Pneumo13_2, VPI 2, VPO1, VPO2, VPO3 & TD2 
#' @param level The column name or vector of column names of the aggregation level of interest. Should be any of Country, Province, District, or Antenne 
#' @param month An integer between 1 to 12 that specifies the cummulative period of months to aggregate date
#' @param accent A logical to specify whether the dataset values contains accented characters. Set to TRUE as default 
#' @param vap_intro A dataframe of VAP introduction dates per health district, as the built-in vap_intro dataset. Used only for VAP1 to VAP4: doses recorded before a district introduced the vaccine, and doses in districts that have not introduced it, are not counted. Set to NULL to count all doses.
#' @param year The calendar year of the data, used to compare with the introduction dates. Default 2026.
#' @importFrom stats aggregate reformulate setNames
#' @return
#' A dataframe with aggregated sums of vaccinated between 
#' @export
#'
#' @examples
vaccine_sums <- function(data, vaccine, level, month = 1, accent = TRUE, vap_intro = pevrdc::vap_intro, year = 2026) {
  vacc_list <- c(
    "BCG" = "bcg_0_et_11_mois",
    "DTC1" = "dtc_hepb_hib1_0_et_11",
    "DTC3" = "dtc_hepb_hib3_0_et_11",
    "VPO0" = "vpo_0_0_et_11",
    "VAA" = "vaa_0_et_11",
    "VAR1" = "var_1_rr_1_0_et_11",
    "VAR2" = "var_2_rr_2_0_et_11_mois|var_2_rr_2_12_et_23_mois",
    "VPI1" = "vpi_1_0_et_11",
    "VPI2" = "vpi_2_0_et_11",
    "Pneumo13" = "pcv_13__3__0_et_11",
    "Rota1" = "rota_1_0_et_11",
    "Rota2" = "rota_2_0_et_11",
    "Rota3" = "rota_3_0_et_11",
    "VAP1" = "vap_1_0_et_11",
    "VAP2" = "vap_2_0_et_11",
    "VAP3" = "vap_3_0_et_11",
    "VAP4" = "vap_4_0_et_11|vap_4_12_et_23",
    "DTC2" = "dtc_hepb_hib2_0_et_11",
    "Pneumo13_2" = "pcv_13__2__0_et_11",
    "VPO1" = "vpo_1_0_et_11",
    "VPO2" = "vpo_2_0_et_11",
    "VPO3" = "vpo_3_0_et_11",
    "TD2" = "td_[2-5]"
  )

  unit <- c(
    "Country" = "orgunitlevel1", "Province" = "orgunitlevel2", "District" = "orgunitlevel3", "Aire" = "orgunitlevel4",
    "Fosa" = "orgunitlevel5", "Antenne" = "orgunitlevel6"
  )

  vaccine1 <- {if(is.character(deparse1(substitute(vaccine)))) as.character(substitute(vaccine)) else deparse1(substitute(vaccine))}

  level1 <- eval(substitute(level), stats::setNames(as.list(unit), names(unit)), parent.frame())


  stopifnot(length(vaccine1) == 1, !is.null(data), vaccine1 %in% names(vacc_list), all(level1 %in% unit), !is.null(level1), !is.null(vaccine1))
  
  if(month < 1 || month > 12)
    stop("month should be between 1 and 12")
  
  if(accent)
    data <- correct_accent(data)

  level <- level1
  vacc_name <- vaccine1
  vaccine <- vacc_list[vaccine1]

  if (!is.null(vap_intro) && vacc_name %in% c("VAP1", "VAP2", "VAP3", "VAP4")) {
    start_month <- vap_start_month(data[["orgunitlevel3"]], vap_intro, year)
  } else {
    start_month <- NULL
  }


  data <- do.call(cbind, list(data["periodname"], data[level], Map(as.numeric, data[grepl(vaccine, colnames(data))])))
  if (!is.null(start_month)) data$vap_start <- start_month


  # removing all NAs
  data[is.na(data)] <- 0
  # Calculating the period

  syst_time <- Sys.getlocale("LC_TIME")

  Sys.setlocale(category = "LC_TIME", locale = "English_United States.utf8")


  period <- c(
    "Janvier" = 1, "Fevrier" = 2, "Mars" = 3, "Avril" = 4, "Mai" = 5, "Juin" = 6, "Juillet" = 7,
    "Aout" = 8, "Septembre" = 9, "Octobre" = 10, "Novembre" = 11, "Decembre" = 12
  )
  period_eng <- c(
    "January" = 1, "February" = 2, "March" = 3, "April" = 4, "May" = 5, "June" = 6, "July" = 7,
    "August" = 8, "September" = 9, "October" = 10, "November" = 11, "December" = 12
  )
  # Robust month number from a French or English month label, with or
  # without accented characters ("Août 2026") or mojibake ("AoÃ»t 2026").
  .month_number <- function(x) {
    key4 <- c(
      "janv" = 1, "janu" = 1, "fevr" = 2, "febr" = 2, "mars" = 3, "marc" = 3,
      "avri" = 4, "apri" = 4, "mai" = 5, "may" = 5, "juin" = 6, "june" = 6,
      "juil" = 7, "july" = 7, "aout" = 8, "augu" = 8, "sept" = 9,
      "octo" = 10, "nove" = 11, "dece" = 12
    )
    corr <- c(
      "\u00C3\u00A0" = "a", "\u00C3\u00A2" = "a", "\u00C3\u00A4" = "a", "\u00C3\u00A7" = "c",
      "\u00C3\u00A8" = "e", "\u00C3\u00A9" = "e", "\u00C3\u00AA" = "e", "\u00C3\u00AB" = "e",
      "\u00C3\u00AC" = "i", "\u00C3\u00AE" = "i", "\u00C3\u00AF" = "i",
      "\u00C3\u00B2" = "o", "\u00C3\u00B4" = "o", "\u00C3\u00B6" = "o",
      "\u00C3\u00B9" = "u", "\u00C3\u00BB" = "u", "\u00C3\u00BC" = "u",
      "\u00C0" = "A", "\u00C2" = "A", "\u00C4" = "A", "\u00C7" = "C",
      "\u00C8" = "E", "\u00C9" = "E", "\u00CA" = "E", "\u00CB" = "E",
      "\u00CE" = "I", "\u00CF" = "I", "\u00D4" = "O", "\u00D6" = "O",
      "\u00D9" = "U", "\u00DB" = "U", "\u00DC" = "U",
      "\u00E0" = "a", "\u00E2" = "a", "\u00E4" = "a", "\u00E7" = "c",
      "\u00E8" = "e", "\u00E9" = "e", "\u00EA" = "e", "\u00EB" = "e",
      "\u00EC" = "i", "\u00EE" = "i", "\u00EF" = "i",
      "\u00F2" = "o", "\u00F4" = "o", "\u00F6" = "o",
      "\u00F9" = "u", "\u00FB" = "u", "\u00FC" = "u"
    )
    for (i in seq_along(corr)) x <- gsub(names(corr)[i], corr[i], x)
    letters_only <- gsub("[^a-zA-Z]", "", x)
    unname(key4[tolower(substr(letters_only, 1, 4))])
  }
  if (all(nchar(as.character(data[["periodname"]])) == 10)) {
    data[, "periodname"] <- as.Date(data[["periodname"]])
    data$period <- period_eng[format(data$periodname, "%B")]
  } else {
    pn <- as.character(data[["periodname"]]); upn <- unique(pn); data$period <- .month_number(upn)[match(pn, upn)]
  }
  if (anyNA(data$period)) {
    bad <- unique(as.character(data[["periodname"]][is.na(data$period)]))
    stop("Unrecognized reporting period(s): ", paste(utils::head(bad, 5), collapse = "; "),
         ". Month labels should contain French or English month names, e.g. 'Janvier 2026' or 'Août 2026'.")
  }
  
  data <- subset(data, period <= month)

  on.exit(Sys.setlocale(category = "LC_TIME", locale = syst_time))

  data$vaccsum <- Reduce(`+`, data[, grepl(vaccine, colnames(data)), drop = FALSE])
  if (!is.null(start_month)) data$vaccsum[data$period < data$vap_start] <- 0

  vacc_agg <- stats::aggregate(stats::reformulate(level, response = "vaccsum"), data = data, FUN = sum)


  names(vacc_agg)[names(vacc_agg) == "vaccsum"] <- vacc_name

  return(vacc_agg)
}




```

```{r function-agg_pop}
#' A function that aggregates the immunization population tallies of DRC per organization level using built-in 2025 population dataset
#'
#' @param var Column name of the variable containing the population numbers. For the pops dataset monthly targets immunization use naissance_mois_ajust or survivant_mois_ajust. For surveillance use population_totale  
#' @param group The organization level orgunitlevel1 for country, orgunitlevel2 for province, orgunitlevel3 for district and orgunitlevel6 for antennes
#' @param month A numeric value between 1 and 12 to specify the number of months for immunization targets
#' @param pops A dataframe with population data 
#'
#' @return
#' A dataframe of aggregated populations 
#' @export
#'
#' @examples
agg_pop <- function(var, group, month = 1, pops) {

  agg_pop_q(substitute(var), substitute(group), month, pops = pops)
}


#' A version of agg_pop that does not use NSE, more convenient to use within other functions. Variables arguments are characters
#'
#' @param var Column name of the variable containing the population numbers. For the pops dataset monthly targets immunization use naissance_mois_ajust or survivant_mois_ajust. For surveillance use population_totale  
#' @param group The organization level orgunitlevel1 for country, orgunitlevel2 for province, orgunitlevel3 for district and orgunitlevel6 for antennes
#' @param month A numeric value between 1 and 12 to specify the number of months for immunization targets
#' @param pops A dataframe with population data
#' @importFrom stats aggregate reformulate
#' @return
#' A dataframe of aggregated populations 
#' @export
#'

agg_pop_2 <- function(var, group, month = 1, pops) {
  # --- Argument checks ---
  stopifnot(is.character(var), length(var) == 1)
  stopifnot(is.character(group), length(group) >= 1)
  stopifnot(is.numeric(month), month >= 1, month <= 12)
  stopifnot(var %in% names(pops))
  stopifnot(all(group %in% names(pops)))

  # --- Aggregate ---
  agg_data <- stats::aggregate(
    stats::reformulate(group, response = var),
    data = pops,
    FUN = sum
  )

  # --- Apply month multiplier when appropriate ---
  if (!grepl("totale", var))
    agg_data[[var]] <- agg_data[[var]] * month

  return(agg_data)
}


#' Core of agg_pop not exported. A function that aggregates the immunization population tallies of DRC per organization level using built-in 2025 population dataset
#' @param var Column name of the variable containing the population numbers. For the pops dataset monthly targets immunization use naissance_mois_ajust or survivant_mois_ajust. For surveillance use population_totale  
#' @param group The organization level orgunitlevel1 for country, orgunitlevel2 for province, orgunitlevel3 for district and orgunitlevel6 for antennes
#' @param month A numeric value between 1 and 12 to specify the number of months for immunization targets
#' @param pops  A dataframe with population data
#' @importFrom stats aggregate reformulate setNames
#' @return
#' A dataframe of aggregated populations 
agg_pop_q <- function(var, group, month = 1, pops) {

  var1 <- {if(is.character(var)) as.character(var) else eval(var, stats::setNames(as.list(names(pops)), names(pops)), parent.frame())}
  group1 <- eval(group, stats::setNames(as.list(names(pops)), names(pops)), parent.frame())
  
   if(month < 1 || month > 12)
    stop("month should be between 1 and 12")
  
  
  stopifnot(is.numeric(pops[[var1]]))

  agg_data <- stats::aggregate(
    stats::reformulate(group1, response = var1),
    data = pops,
    FUN = sum
  )

  if(!grepl("totale",var1))
    agg_data[[var1]] <-agg_data[[var1]] * month

  return(agg_data)
}
```

# Vaccine Coverage 




```{r function-vaccine_coverage}
#' A function to compute the cummulative monthly vaccine coverage  per organization levels using DHIS2 exported data
#'
#' @param data Dataframe, usually the DHIS2 immunization dataframe already aggregated
#' @param vaccine Column name of the vaccine of interest. Should be one of the following: BCG, DTC1, DTC3, VPO0, VAA, VAR1, VAR2, VPI1, VPI2, Pneumo13, Rota1, Rota2, Rota3, VAP1, VAP2, VAP3, VAP4, DTC2, Pneumo13_2, VPI 2, VPO1, VPO2, VPO3 & TD2 
#' @param level The column name or vector of column names of the aggregation level of interest. Should be any of Country, Province, District or Antenne 
#' @param month An integer between 1 to 12 that specifies the cummulative period of months to aggregate date
#' @param pops An aggregated dataset of target populations.
#' @param vap_intro A dataframe of VAP introduction dates per health district, as the built-in vap_intro dataset. Used only for VAP1 to VAP4: the target population of a district only counts the months since it introduced the vaccine, and districts that have not introduced it have no target (coverage NA). Set to NULL to use all months for all districts.
#' @param year The calendar year of the data, used to compare with the introduction dates. Default 2026.
#' @importFrom stats aggregate reformulate setNames
#' @return
#' A dataframe with vaccines coverage 
#' For VAP1 to VAP4 the target population columns are prefixed with vap_ (vap_survivants_mois_admin, vap_survivant_mois_ajust) because they only cover the months since introduction, so they differ from the targets of the other vaccines and tables can be merged by key without losing rows.
#' @export
#'
#' @examples

vaccine_coverage <- function(data, vaccine, level, month = 1, pops, vap_intro = pevrdc::vap_intro, year = 2026) {
  vac <- c(
    "BCG", "DTC1", "DTC3", "VPO0", "VAA", "VAR1", "VAR2", "VPI1",
    "VPI2", "Pneumo13", "Rota1", "Rota2", "Rota3", "VAP1", "VAP2",
    "VAP3", "VAP4", "DTC2", "Pneumo13_2", "VPI 2", "VPO1", "VPO2",
    "VPO3", "TD2"
  )
  unit <- c(
    "Country" = "orgunitlevel1", "Province" = "orgunitlevel2", "District" = "orgunitlevel3", "Aire" = "orgunitlevel4",
    "Fosa" = "orgunitlevel5", "Antenne" = "orgunitlevel6"
  )

  level1 <- eval(substitute(level), stats::setNames(as.list(unit), names(unit)), parent.frame())

  vaccine1 <-{if(is.character(deparse1(substitute(vaccine)))) as.character(substitute(vaccine)) else deparse1(substitute(vaccine))}

  vaccine <- vaccine1

  stopifnot(is.numeric(month), !is.null(data), vaccine %in% vac, vaccine %in% colnames(data), all(level1 %in% unit))

  level <- level1



  data <- stats::aggregate(stats::reformulate(level, response = vaccine), FUN = sum, data = data)


  if (vaccine %in% c("BCG", "VPO0", "TD2")) {
    num_vars <- c("naissance_mois_admin", "naissance_mois_ajust")
  } else {
    num_vars <- c("survivants_mois_admin", "survivant_mois_ajust")
  }

  is_vap <- !is.null(vap_intro) && vaccine %in% c("VAP1", "VAP2", "VAP3", "VAP4")
  pop_month <- month
  if (is_vap) {
    active_months <- pmax(0, month - vap_start_month(pops[["orgunitlevel3"]], vap_intro, year) + 1)
    pops[num_vars] <- pops[num_vars] * active_months
    pop_month <- 1
  }

  pop1 <- agg_pop_2(num_vars[1],level, month = pop_month, pops = pops)
  pop2 <- agg_pop_2(num_vars[2],level, month = pop_month, pops = pops)


  populations <- merge(pop1, pop2, by = level)



  merged_data <- merge(data, populations, by = level)

  dropped <- nrow(data) - nrow(merged_data)
  if (dropped > 0) {
    warning(dropped, " unit(s) have no matching target population and were dropped from the coverage table. Check that names in the data and in pops are spelled identically.", call. = FALSE)
  }
  
  
    if(vaccine == "VAR2"|vaccine == "VAP4"){
      
        merged_data[[paste0(vaccine, "_admin")]] <- round(100 * merged_data[[vaccine]] / (merged_data[[num_vars[1]]]* 0.97), 2)
        merged_data[[paste0(vaccine, "_ajust")]] <- round(100 * merged_data[[vaccine]] / (merged_data[[num_vars[2]]]*0.97), 2)
    
    }else{
      
  merged_data[[paste0(vaccine, "_admin")]] <- round(100 * merged_data[[vaccine]] / merged_data[[num_vars[1]]], 2)
  merged_data[[paste0(vaccine, "_ajust")]] <- round(100 * merged_data[[vaccine]] / merged_data[[num_vars[2]]], 2)
      
  }




  if (is_vap) {
    for (s in c("_admin", "_ajust")) {
      v <- merged_data[[paste0(vaccine, s)]]
      v[!is.finite(v)] <- NA
      merged_data[[paste0(vaccine, s)]] <- v
    }
    names(merged_data)[names(merged_data) %in% num_vars] <- paste0("vap_", num_vars)
  }

  implausible <- sum(merged_data[[paste0(vaccine, "_admin")]] > 150, na.rm = TRUE)
  if (implausible > 0) {
    warning(implausible, " unit(s) have an administrative ", vaccine, " coverage above 150%: check for data entry errors in the numerator or for an under-estimated target population.", call. = FALSE)
  }

  if(vaccine == "DTC1"){
    merged_data[["zero_dose_admin"]] <- round(merged_data[[num_vars[1]]] - merged_data[[vaccine]])
    merged_data[["zero_dose_ajust"]] <- round(merged_data[[num_vars[2]]] - merged_data[[vaccine]])

  }
  


  return(merged_data)
}


```

# Cleaning names

Each of them will be inflated in a different file, provided that there is a level-1 or level-2 section title to separate from previous functions.
-->

## Use sub-functions in the same chunk

```{r function-clean_dhis_names}
#' A function that removes DRC DHIS prefixes and suffixes 
#'
#' @param data The dataset containing variables to be cleaned  
#' @param column The column containing values to be cleaned espcially organization levels of DRC EPI
#' @param has_prefix An integer specifying the number of characters of the prefix to be removed. Set to 0 if no prefix
#' @param suffix A character value that specifies the suffix to be removed
#'
#' @return
#' A dataframe with cleaned names
#' @export
#'
#' @examples
clean_dhis_names <- function(data, column, has_prefix = 2, 
                             suffix = "(Province|Zone de Sant[e\u00e9]|Aire de Sant[e\u00e9]|Centre de Sant[e\u00e9])"){
 clean_dhis_names_q(data, substitute(column), has_prefix, suffix)

}



#' Core of clean_dhis_names not exported.#'
#' @param data The dataset containing variables to be cleaned  
#' @param column The column containing values to be cleaned espcially organization levels of DRC EPI
#' @param has_prefix An integer specifying the number of characters of the prefix to be removed. Set to 0 if no prefix
#' @param suffix A character value that specifies the suffix to be removed
#'
#' @return
#' A dataframe with cleaned names

clean_dhis_names_q <- function(data, column, has_prefix = 2,
                               suffix = "(Province|Zone de Sant[e\u00e9]|Aire de Sant[e\u00e9]|Centre de Sant[e\u00e9])"){

  column1 <- eval(column, setNames(as.list(names(data)), names(data)), parent.frame())

  column <- column1

  stopifnot(!is.null(data), !is.null(column), is.character(column), is.character(suffix), is.numeric(has_prefix), length(column) == 1)

  if (!column %in% names(data)) stop("Column not found in data: ", column)

  has_prefix <- as.integer(has_prefix)

  suffix <- gsub("([.|()\\^{}+$*?]|\\[|\\]|\\\\)", "\\\\\\1", suffix)

  string <- paste0("(^[A-Za-z]", "{", has_prefix,"})|(", suffix,"$)")

  data[[column]] <- trimws(gsub(string, "", data[[column]], perl = TRUE), "both")

  if(suffix == "") warning("No suffix was trimmed")

  if(has_prefix == 0) warning("No prefix was trimmed")

  return(data)


}



#' A function that removes DRC's DHIS 2 prefixes and suffixes  from a vector
#'
#' @param x A character vector to be cleaned especially organization levels of DRC EPI. More convenient to use within other functions
#' @param has_prefix An integer specifying the number of characters of the prefix to be removed. Set to 0 if no prefix
#' @param suffix A character value that specifies the suffix to be removed
#'
#' @return
#' A character vector
#' @export
#'



clean_names_dhis <- function(x, has_prefix = 2, 
                             suffix = "(Province|Zone de Sant[e\u00e9]|Aire de Sant[e\u00e9]|Centre de Sant[e\u00e9])") {
  stopifnot(is.character(x), !is.null(x),  is.character(suffix), is.numeric(has_prefix))
  pattern <- paste0("(^[A-Za-z]{", has_prefix, "}\\s*)|(\\s*", suffix, "$)")

  cleaned <- trimws(gsub(pattern, "", x, perl = TRUE))

  return(cleaned)
}





```

```{r examples-clean_dhis_names}

datafile <- system.file(c("pop2025.RDS"), package = "pevrdc")

vacc <- readRDS(datafile)
clean_dhis_names(vacc, column = orgunitlevel2, has_prefix = 2, suffix = "Province")

clean_names_dhis(vacc$orgunitlevel2,  has_prefix = 2,
                 suffix = "(Province|Zone de Sant[e\u00e9]|Aire de Sant[e\u00e9]|Centre de Sant[e\u00e9])")
```

```{r tests-clean_dhis_names}
datafile <- system.file(c("pop2025.RDS"), package = "pevrdc")

pop <- readRDS(datafile)

pop <- clean_dhis_names(pop, column = orgunitlevel3, has_prefix = 2, suffix = "Zone de Sante")




test_that("clean_dhis_names removes all the suffixes", {
  expect_true(sum(grepl("(Zone de Sante)$", pop$orgunitlevel1)) == 0)
})
```

# Antenne


```{r function-add_antennes}
#' A function that adds DRC antennes to a dataset not having them
#'
#' @param data A dataset with no variable containing antennes, usually DHIS 2 datasets  
#' @param province A Column with province
#' @param zone A column with health zones
#' @param rename_antenne A logical to indicate renaming antennes following DHIS 2 standard 
#'
#' @return
#' A dataframe with a variable with antennes
#' @export
#'



add_antennes <- function(data, province, zone, rename_antenne = TRUE) {
  
  stopifnot(!is.null(data), is.data.frame(data))
  

 
  level <- c(deparse1(substitute(province)), deparse1(substitute(zone)))
  
  antennes <- get("antennes", "package:pevrdc")
  colnames(antennes) <- c(level[1], "antenne", level[2])
  data$zs <- trimws(gsub("^[A-Za-z]{2}|Zone de Sant[e\u00e9]$", "", data[[level[2]]]), "both")
  data$prov<- trimws(gsub("^[A-Za-z]{2}|Province$", "", data[[level[1]]]), "both")
    
    merged_data <- merge(data, antennes, by.x = c("prov","zs"), by.y = level)
    
    merged_data$zs <- NULL
    merged_data$prov <- NULL
    

  
  if (rename_antenne) {
    merged_data$orgunitlevel6 <- merged_data$antenne
    
    merged_data$antenne <- NULL
    
    cat("Antenne column is renamed orgunitlevel6")
  }
  
  
  return(merged_data)
}





```



# Outbreak classification





```{r function-is_outbreak}
#' This is function returns TRUE after n successive TRUE and FALSE otherwise. This is a convenient function to classify areas with outbreak following consecutive
#' positive cases of diseases recorded within n weeks.
#' @param x an ordered logical vector 
#' @param nwk a numeric value that specifies the window frame for the assessment of consecutive logical values of x 
#' @return
#' A logical vecor of similar length with x
#' @export
#'
#' @examples

is_outbreak <- function(x, nwk = 4) {
  stopifnot(is.logical(x)|is.numeric(x))
  if(is.numeric(x)){
    x <- as.logical(x)
    warning("x was coerced to logical")
  }
  if (anyNA(x)){
    warning("NA values present; treated as FALSE")
    x[is.na(x)] <- FALSE}

  sapply(seq_along(x), function(i) {
    sum(x[max((i - nwk + 1),0):i]) >= 3
  })
}



```

```{r function-district_epi}
#' This is function is wrapper around is_outbreak to identify districts with an outbreak. 
#' @param df A dataset with a weekly number of cases or a logical indication of a case detected
#' @param district A variable containing districts names
#' @param wk A numeric variable specifying the successive week numbers 
#' @param status A logical or numeric variable with either indication of case recorded or the number of cases
#' @param nwk A numeric value that specifies the window frame for the assessment of consecutive logical values of x 
#' @param sorted A logical value to specify whether the dataset is ordered per week and district
#' @param pre_yr A logical value to specify whether dataset contains data from the previous year
#' @param year A numeric variable containing the year of the data
#' @return
#' A dataframe with an additional logical variable epi_status
#' @export
#'
#' @examples
district_epi <- function(df, district, wk, status, nwk = 4, sorted = FALSE, pre_yr = FALSE, year = NULL){

  district <- deparse1(substitute(district))

  wk <- deparse1(substitute(wk))

  status <- deparse1(substitute(status))

  if(!is.null(year))
    year <- deparse1(substitute(year))

  stopifnot(!is.null(df), !is.null(district), !is.null(wk), !is.null(status))


  if(!sorted)
    df <- df[order(df[[district]], df[[wk]]),]

  if(pre_yr){
    if(is.null(year))
      stop("year must be specified if pre_yr is set to TRUE")
    yr <- sort(unique(as.numeric(df[[year]])))
    if (length(yr) != 2)
      stop("pre_yr = TRUE requires exactly two distinct years in the dataset.")
    if((yr[2] - 1)!= yr[1])
      stop("Years are not consecutive")

    pre <- df[df[[year]] == yr[1]]

    current <- df[df[[year]] == yr[2]]

    pre <- pre[order(pre[[district]], pre[[wk]]),]

    current <- current[order(current[[district]], current[[wk]]),]

    df <- rbind(pre, current)}



  sp <- split(df, df[[district]])


  for (i in 1:length(sp)){

    sp[[i]][["epi_status"]] <- is_outbreak(sp[[i]][[status]], nwk = nwk)

  }

  epi_districts <- do.call(rbind, sp)

  row.names(epi_districts) <- NULL

  return(epi_districts)


}


```
